interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta exibida "Eight sixths equals how many thirds?"; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 2, uma acima da outra: na Linha 1 a fração dada já está marcada pelo tutor; na Linha 2 o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividir (campo de denominador + confirmar) e marca o ponto da fração equivalente; à direita das retas, a igualdade entre as duas frações é mostrada em caixas: as da esquerda vêm preenchidas e, na da direita, o aluno digita o NUMERADOR (o denominador alvo já aparece); há também um seletor de comparação ("≟", "=", "≠") entre as duas frações; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir a Linha 2, marcar o ponto, digitar o numerador, comparar, concluir).

Linha 2 — reta numérica com rótulos, onde o aluno divide e marca a fração equivalente
seletor de comparação entre as duas frações: "≟", "=", "≠"
campo numérico onde o aluno digita o NUMERADOR da fração equivalente
campo numérico do denominador da Linha 2 sem rótulos + botão de confirmar
campo numérico do denominador da Linha 1 (quantas partes) + botão de confirmar
campo numérico do denominador da Linha 2 + botão de confirmar
campo de texto do numerador exibido pelo tutor (não é do aluno)
imagem/rótulo do sinal de comparação entre as frações

hints.message: The denominator names the number of equal parts in one whole.
Read the requested unit, enter that number in the denominator field, and then confirm.
The line must show thirds, not sixths.
Enter the number of parts that corresponds to the word thirds, then press the confirmation control.

misconceptions.description: Aluno ignora a unidade solicitada (terços) e replica o denominador da fração original.
misconceptions.feedback: You entered 6, which keeps the original sixths. The instruction asks you to divide Line 2 into thirds.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta as marcações (hastes) da reta em vez dos intervalos entre elas.

nodes.description: Mark on Line 2 the point equal to the marked point on Line 1.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions name the same location even when the parts have different sizes.
Use the marked point on Line 1 as a reference, then count thirds from zero on Line 2.
The target lies one whole and some additional thirds from zero.
On Line 2, move past the first whole and select the interval that has the same endpoint as the mark for 8/6.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator of the fraction shown by your mark on Line 2.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator of the fraction shown by your mark on Line 2.

hints.message: The numerator counts how many parts of the stated size are reached.
Count the thirds from zero, including the thirds after passing one whole.
There are three thirds in one whole, plus one more third.
Add the three thirds that make one whole to the additional third at the marked point, then enter that count.

misconceptions.description: O aluno tenta manter a diferença constante entre numerador e denominador.
misconceptions.feedback: You subtracted the denominator change from the numerator. Equivalent fractions use the same location and proportion, not a constant difference.

misconceptions.description: O aluno responde com o valor do denominador (3) no campo do numerador.
misconceptions.feedback: You entered the denominator as the numerator. The denominator is 3, while the numerator counts the thirds reached by the mark.

misconceptions.description: Aluno mantém o numerador da fração original e apenas altera o denominador.
misconceptions.feedback: You kept the original numerator without recounting the parts on Line 2. Count the thirds that reach the same location.

nodes.description: Set the comparison selector to show that the two fractions are equal.
nodes.instruction: Set the comparison selector to show that the two fractions are equal.

hints.message: Equivalent fractions represent the same amount.
Compare the locations of the two marks rather than comparing the numerals separately.
The marks line up at the same point on the number lines.
Choose the comparison symbol that means both fractions have exactly the same value.

nodes.description: Click Done to submit the completed equivalent-fraction comparison.
nodes.instruction: Click Done to submit the completed equivalent-fraction comparison.

hints.message: Before submitting, check that both fractions describe the same point.
Review the denominator, the marked point, the numerator, and the comparison sign.
Make sure Line 2 is divided into thirds and the right-hand fraction uses the point aligned with 8/6.
When every field and mark is complete, press the Done button to submit the comparison.
